climbing_route.label: Snow Dome to the false-summit saddle
climbing_route.notes: From Snow Dome (6,600 ft) head south-southeast through one of two passes flanking the five-fingered false summit east of the true summit, dropping into the sharp saddle between the false summit and the now-visible true summit pyramid. Route-finding through the rock islands and false-summit passes is the crux of the upper mountain in flat light; a large crevasse near Crystal Pass, usually crossed on a snow bridge, is a key hazard on the glacier portion.

climbing_route.label: East face ramps
climbing_route.notes: Instead of the shortest line to the base of the summit rock, this variation climbs a series of ramps angling up and across the east face of the summit pyramid.

climbing_route.label: Final summit step
climbing_route.notes: The ramps join the final Class 4/5.4 step to the top.

climbing_route.label: Climbers' path onto the southeast slopes
climbing_route.notes: Continue a short distance past Pinnacle Saddle (about 5,920-5,960 ft) and look for a climbers' path branching right (west); it crosses a flat rocky shelf holding a seasonal tarn, where a fork continues straight toward Denman - instead bear left (south/uphill) onto the boot path climbing the open, rocky southeast-facing slopes. Unmaintained, loose in spots, and the tread is thin. A lingering snowfield often crosses the boot path near the saddle into July - either kick steps straight up it or skirt left on the rockier tread; both options rejoin near the top.

climbing_route.label: Summit scramble
climbing_route.notes: A short class 2-3 scramble - brief hands-on-rock moves, some loose blocks, mild exposure - gains the last few hundred feet to the 6,374 ft summit.

climbing_route.label: Quien Sabe Glacier, lower half
climbing_route.notes: From high camp, rope up around 6,700 ft and make a rising traverse near the cliffs below Sharkfin Tower, picking a line up the Quien Sabe Glacier while avoiding crevasses; two common ascent lines (a left-side line and a more direct one) merge partway up.

climbing_route.label: Bergschrund to the Boston-Sahale col
climbing_route.notes: Expect to navigate a bergschrund via snow bridges around 7,600 ft and again near 8,100 ft, where large open crevasses flank the route on both sides in late season, before climbing to the Boston-Sahale col.

climbing_route.label: Snow traverse from the col
climbing_route.notes: From the col, a short but exposed snow traverse leads to the base of the summit block; crampons and axe recommended even late season.

climbing_route.label: Summit block
climbing_route.notes: Finished with class 3-4 scrambling to the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Sahale Glacier to the summit pyramid
climbing_route.notes: Above Sahale Glacier Camp, rope up for glacier travel and ascend directly to the southwest base of the summit pyramid. The Sahale Glacier is small and generally low crevasse hazard compared to nearby glaciers, but should not be crossed unroped without current beta, especially late season.

climbing_route.label: Steep snow and rock to the summit ledge
climbing_route.notes: A short, exposed stretch of steep snow and 3rd-4th class rock leads to a ledge just below the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Summit chimney move
climbing_route.notes: Finished by a short, awkward chimney-like move (about 5.0) onto the summit block.

climbing_route.label: Traverse to the east side and onto the glacier
climbing_route.notes: From the Cyclone Lake camp, traverse below or over Peak 5,860 heading toward Snowking's east side, then gain the Snowking Glacier proper.

climbing_route.label: Snowking Glacier
climbing_route.notes: Roughly 1,900 ft over about 1.3 miles to the summit. In late season a straightforward snow/heather slope, but by mid-to-late summer the glacier opens up with exposed blue ice and real crevasses - rope up for glacier travel and carry basic crevasse-rescue gear rather than treating it as a snow plod.

climbing_route.label: Summit block
climbing_route.notes: A final short scree/talus traverse and easy class 2-3 scramble gains the broad summit block at 7,433 ft.

climbing_route.label: Off-trail scramble to the dividing ridge
climbing_route.notes: Leave the Glacier Basin Trail (~4,400-4,680 ft) and scramble to the dividing ridge. Confirm you're on the correct ridge before committing, since parties from this trailhead often end up on the neighboring East Wilmans Spire, a separate roped climb.

climbing_route.label: Summit block
climbing_route.notes: The final summit block is rated Class 4 per the 1970 first-ascent record, not a pure walk-up - expect short, exposed scrambling moves near the top.

climbing_route.label: Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier to Klawatti Col
climbing_route.notes: From high camp the route continues as sustained glacier travel rather than a trail: cross the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier, where crevasses are worst near Eldorado's east ridge - stay roped and probe - then traverse the upper Inspiration Glacier at ~7,800 ft to Klawatti Col. Crevasse fall on all three glaciers gets worse as the season progresses and snow bridges soften, and route-finding is difficult in flat light or whiteout on the open ice cap.

climbing_route.label: Klawatti's north ridge along the upper McAllister Glacier
climbing_route.notes: Pass Klawatti Peak on its left through the col and follow Klawatti's north ridge along the upper McAllister Glacier about 0.4 miles to a break in the ridge at ~7,900 ft, the Klawatti-Austera col/notch. From camp this traverse runs roughly 3 miles crossing three glacier basins and two cols, with about 1,280 ft of ascent and 592 ft of descent over 2.8 miles, ~4 hours one-way. Loose rock ('choss') on any exposed rock sections; a genuinely committing and remote setting with long retreat times.

climbing_route.label: Klawatti-Austera notch (crux)
climbing_route.notes: A moat gap at the col that often requires careful stemming or a short rappel to get down onto the upper Klawatti Glacier before the final traverse to Austera's base.

climbing_route.label: Cliff band below the summit massif (crux)
climbing_route.notes: Around 4,900-5,200 ft, parties look for a ramp/notch line rather than the more direct gully - a moat-like gap has been found there and is best avoided. The rock is mossy and loose in spots, occasionally icy where snow meets rock; a short hand-line is sometimes used here by less experienced climbers.

climbing_route.label: Descending traverse east to the ridge
climbing_route.notes: A short descending traverse east through overgrown brush and devil's club near 5,200 ft regains the ridge above treeline.

climbing_route.label: Snow and granite slabs to the east ridge
climbing_route.notes: A straightforward snow climb and crossing of low-angle granite slabs to the east ridge - an easy, minimally-exposed Class 2-3 scramble toward the summit.

climbing_route.label: Final slab traverse below the summit cliffs
climbing_route.notes: Just below the summit cliffs, a roughly 30-foot traverse of exposed but positive Class 2-3 slabs with a bad runout, slippery when wet and often protected with a hand line by cautious parties.
